operational_simulation.organization_and_actor: Municipal or state social-policy administration; program manager, SUAS coordination, and evaluation team
processes: choose outreach intensity for Cadastro Unico update and benefit-access campaigns
compare light-touch messaging, assisted scheduling, mobile service, and active-search visits
evaluate which intervention changes service access without automating eligibility
operational_simulation.deterministic_baseline: eligibility rules, universal communications, territorial prioritization, scheduled mobile service, structured active-search protocols, phased rollout, and human casework
operational_simulation.remaining_gap: estimate heterogeneous causal effects of bounded outreach alternatives rather than predicting vulnerability or eligibility

training_data.observation_unit: eligible household or territorial cohort at the moment an outreach intervention is assigned
training_data.input_data: only pre-intervention administrative, territorial, channel-access, and prior-service-contact attributes permitted for policy evaluation
training_data.target_or_reward: verified registration update, completed service access, or program take-up within a prespecified window
training_data.label_source: prospective experiment or governed phased rollout with recorded intervention assignment and later administrative outcome
training_data.expected_volume: unknown; must be established by the participating program and municipality
training_data.class_balance: unknown; depends on baseline take-up and the selected outcome window
training_data.historical_coverage: current administrative history does not reliably preserve treatment assignment, propensity, adherence, and comparable untreated outcomes
training_data.train_validation_split: prospective time- and municipality-separated evaluation; randomization or a defensible quasi-experimental design preferred
training_data.leakage_risks: using post-contact updates, completed appointments, benefit decisions, later caseworker notes, or outcomes recorded after assignment
training_data.representativeness_risks: municipality capacity, connectivity, territorial access, program rules, disability, language, and channel availability vary materially
training_data.feedback_loop: program evaluators review aggregate treatment effects, subgroup uncertainty, non-response, and unintended access barriers
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: no automated eligibility, denial, individual vulnerability scoring, punitive targeting, or use beyond the defined public-policy purpose
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: use universal or rule-based outreach and run a bounded randomized or phased evaluation before any uplift model

portfolio_coherence.material_differentiation: none proven; the causal capability would be an evaluation method for outreach policy, not a distinct operational solution architecture

existing_landscape.notes: Brazil already has integrated Cadastro Unico infrastructure, professional active-search workflows, and formal public-policy evaluation mechanisms. International field experiments show simple universal outreach may outperform precise targeting, weakening the need for an uplift product before prospective local experimentation.
